situation:
You are the promotion manager for LANTERN STREET LANGUAGE STUDIO, an adult language school that teaches conversational Spanish, Italian and Japanese to working adults who are getting ready to travel. The founder (judge) opened the studio eleven years ago, has run it profitably for the last seven, and plans to sell the business and step away at the end of this year.

Almost every new student arrives by word of mouth. Graduates tell coworkers and friends where they learned enough Italian to order dinner in Rome, and COASTLINE TOURS, a regional travel operator, sends its own travelers to the studio's four-week conversation course before their trips. A signed two-year exclusive agreement holds that arrangement together: COASTLINE refers its travelers, and the studio promotes no other travel company in its classrooms, its emails or its social posts.

HARBOR RIDGE PARTNERS, an outside investor, has offered the capital to build a national self-study app and to price the studio well for sale. The investor's growth plan sells that app through WAYPOINT, a large online travel booking platform that puts the studio's courses in front of far more travelers than COASTLINE reaches. Promoting WAYPOINT breaks the exclusive agreement and ends the COASTLINE referrals that fill the classrooms today.

Turning the investor down keeps the COASTLINE agreement and the graduates' word of mouth intact, but the studio stays at one classroom, builds no app, and the founder (judge) sells a single location for less. The founder (judge) wants your analysis of which promotional mix and which product mix the studio should carry into the sale, and how the courses would be positioned either way.

Present your recommendation to the founder (judge) in a meeting at the studio, together with the reasoning behind it and what you would say to COASTLINE TOURS about it. The founder (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the founder (judge) of LANTERN STREET LANGUAGE STUDIO. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You built the studio from one rented classroom eleven years ago, and you are selling it and stepping away at the end of this year. You want to hear which way the promotion manager would go — the capital from HARBOR RIDGE PARTNERS and the app sold through WAYPOINT, or the exclusive agreement with COASTLINE TOURS — and you want to hear how the studio's courses would be promoted and positioned under that choice.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: What would you say to COASTLINE TOURS about this decision?
When would you tell them, and who should be in that conversation?
